Definition: from G575 and ἵημι (to send; an intensive form of εἶμι, to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow):--cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up.
BiblicalUsage: To send away, to let go — forgive us our debts, the master forgiving his servant's whole debt out of pity, the woman whose many sins are forgiven because she loved much, and the church given the charge to remit sins or retain them. The word covers letting go of a debt, leaving a boat, and leaving a place, because all of them are a sending away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe forgiveness is the clearest picture of what God did for me: he sent my sins away, as far as the east is from the west, and he did it because of Christ. And I hold that the same sending away is now my own calling toward everyone who owes me anything.
